title: After the guns: winning trust in Bastar
news: The PM said armed Naxals have been wiped out but 'intellectual Naxals' must be defeated; LWE districts have fallen to seven.
syllabus: Good governance; inclusive governance; balancing security and rights
link: Security operations restore order, but legitimacy comes from schools, roads, gram sabhas and respect for tribal rights. The ethical task now is to counter extremist ideas without treating dissent or tribal assertion as disloyalty.
question: "The end of armed insurgency is the beginning of a test of governance." Discuss the ethical responsibilities of administrators in areas freed from Left Wing Extremism.

title: Rules made without asking
news: Maharashtra says FSSAI changed licence thresholds without public consultation and created central inspectors not provided in the Act.
syllabus: Good governance; transparency; rule of law
link: Even a well-intended rule loses legitimacy when made without consultation or beyond the law. The central official's worry, that a state's performance depends on one officer, is a lesson in building institutions that outlast individuals.
question: "Good governance rests on institutions, not individuals." Discuss with reference to regulatory enforcement.

title: Selling the lock and the key
news: AI firms that expose software vulnerabilities could also sell protection against them.
syllabus: Applied ethics: technology; conflict of interest
link: When the same company finds a flaw and sells its fix, incentives may favour exposure over safety. Responsible disclosure and transparency are ethical duties in dual-use technology.
question: Discuss the ethical concerns in the use of artificial intelligence in cyber security.

title: When the ballot audits power
news: American voters handed Congress to the opposition after a President who cast the election as a referendum on himself was seen as wielding unchecked power.
link: Elections are the final form of accountability: power that ignores citizens' everyday concerns, such as the cost of living, is answerable at the ballot box. The editorial's warning, that parties tied to a leader's cult inherit his liabilities, is a lesson in why institutions must rank above individuals.
question: "Accountability is the price of power in a democracy." Discuss with reference to the relationship between leaders and institutions.

title: Autonomy must answer to someone
news: CERT-In requires AI security incidents to be reported within six hours and audits scaled to risk, after AI agents exceeded their authorised tasks.
link: When machines act on their own, responsibility must still rest with people. Traceability, explainability and human oversight are the AI-age versions of the public servant's duty to give reasons and answer for decisions.
question: As AI systems take decisions in administration, how can accountability be ensured? Discuss.

title: Land with consent and clear rules
news: West Bengal's new policy prefers buying and pooling land over acquisition, with a GIS land inventory, online time-stamped allotment and recovery of unused land.
syllabus: Probity in governance; Transparency; Fairness to affected people
link: Singur and Nandigram showed the cost of development without consent. Transparent, rule-based allotment reduces discretion and corruption, while a use-it-or-lose-it clause protects public resources from being hoarded.
question: How can transparency and consent make land acquisition for industry both fair and efficient? Discuss.

title: Selling the gate to public service
news: A former KPSC chairman, accused of leaking answer keys for bribes, was also suspended over the commission's recruitment of his own daughter.
syllabus: Probity in governance; Integrity; Conflict of interest; Impartiality
link: A recruiting body is the gate to public service: when its head sells answer keys and selects his own daughter, it betrays the impartiality and trust on which the whole civil service rests. Corruption at the entry point corrupts every service that follows.
question: "Corruption in public recruitment is the most damaging form of corruption because it corrupts the system at its source." Discuss.

title: Dollar investors, rupee investors
news: Amid calls to cut taxes for foreign investors, the Finance Minister asked: 'If you pitch for dollar investors, what about rupee investors?'
syllabus: Impartiality and non-partisanship; Fairness in public policy
link: Public policy must treat like cases alike: concessions that favour foreign over domestic investors for the same income break fairness and impartiality, even when the aim of attracting capital is legitimate. Good ends do not justify unequal means.
question: "Fairness in public policy means treating like cases alike." Examine with an example from economic policy.

title: Governing on trust
news: The Finance Minister said GST, income tax and other policies are framed on trusting businesses, farmers, taxpayers and citizens: 'That will remain our charter.'
syllabus: Public service values; Trust and citizen-centric governance; Accountability
link: A state that presumes honesty treats citizens as partners, not suspects, cutting harassment and compliance costs. Trust must be paired with accountability, so that honest citizens are freed while the few who abuse trust still face consequences.
question: "Trust-based governance must be balanced with accountability." Discuss with examples.

title: Anticipate, but with care
news: CERT-In is testing an advanced AI model to find software flaws before attackers do, but only on small datasets, wary of exposing sensitive public data.
syllabus: Proactive and anticipatory governance; Prudence; Ethical issues in the use of technology
link: Good administration anticipates threats instead of waiting for them, as CERT-In does by hunting vulnerabilities in advance. Yet it also acts with prudence: the duty to protect citizens' data limits how far a new tool is used. Proactivity with caution is responsible governance.
question: "Proactive governance requires both foresight and prudence." Discuss with reference to the use of emerging technologies by the State.

title: When rules outlive their purpose
news: Nagaland says the Protected Area Permit, framed for a different security era, and its convoluted process now keep tourists away from a peaceful state.
syllabus: Citizen-friendly administration; Efficiency in public service; Form versus substance
link: A rule is a means, not an end: when conditions change, administrators must review whether it still serves its purpose. Delays and last-minute relaxations show form winning over substance, and a citizen-centric administration fixes the process, not just the policy.
question: "Rules that outlive their purpose become obstacles to good governance." Discuss with examples.

title: The State's duty to be knowable
news: A writer proposes that only rules published on one national legal register should be enforceable against citizens.
syllabus: Transparency; Rule of law; Probity in governance; Trust
link: A government that enforces rules citizens cannot find betrays fairness; publishing every obligation is an ethical duty that limits discretion and corruption.
question: "Hidden rules are the soil in which corruption grows." Discuss.
